newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria warns public about possible letter-bombs.
newsitem.headline: Austria warns public about possible letter-bombs.

text.p: Austria asked the public on Sunday to look out for letter-bombs in the Christmas mail, fearing there could be a resurgence of a suspected neo-Nazi campaign that has baffled investigators, Austrian news agency APA said.
The interior ministry said it had not received any specific threat, but asked Austrians to be particularly vigilant during the festive season, the agency said.

Police suspect neo-Nazis have been behind more than 20 letter bombs directed against foreigners and figures linked to immigrant or refugee issues since 1993. Sofar 11 people have been injured, including former Vienna mayor Helmut Zilk.

In October, a group calling itself the Bavarian Liberation Army (BLA) threatened to target eight prominent figures, including Chancellor Franz Vranitzky, prompting tighter security for some of Austria's top politicians.

The group has claimed responsibility for the wave of letter bombs and investigators have linked the BLA to the murder of four gypsies who were killed by a booby-trap bomb attached to a racist sign in February 1995.
The letter bomb attacks spilled over into Germany last year when an assistant of television show host Arabella Kiesbauer, whose father is Ghanaian, sufferd facial injuries in a blast.
